record.context_brief: EMRI probes near SMBH and IMBH environments
record.original_question: Can dark-matter-rich environments near supermassive black holes (SMBHs, about 10^6–10^10 solar masses) and intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs, about 10^3–10^6 solar masses), where PBH abundances may be enhanced, produce extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) signals detectable by LISA?

evidence.quote: they may play key roles as rare IMBH (Intermediate Mass BHs in the range (103−106)M⊙ that may seed both SMBH (Supermassive Black Holes observed in the mass range (106−1010)M⊙ and massive galaxies in the early universe.

And can we use the vicinities of SMBH amd IMBH, most likely rich in dark matter and where PBH abundances are in consequence likely to be enhanced, as potential sources of EMRI signals for experiments such as LISA?

artifact.category_tag: primordial black holes and gravitational-wave detection
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider supermassive black holes (SMBHs) with masses in the range $10^6$–$10^{10}\,M_\odot$ and intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) with masses in the range $10^3$–$10^6\,M_\odot$. Suppose the local environments around such black holes are dark-matter rich, and that a fraction of the dark matter is in the form of primordial black holes (PBHs) of sub-solar to stellar mass, with abundances locally enhanced relative to the cosmological average due to dynamical concentration in these galactic centers. An extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) is the long-duration gravitational-wave signal generated as a stellar-mass compact object slowly inspirals into a much more massive (SMBH or IMBH) central black hole, and the planned space-based gravitational-wave observatory LISA is sensitive to such signals in the millihertz band.

Determine, under astrophysically motivated models for PBH dark matter density profiles (e.g. spike or cusp profiles) around SMBHs and IMBHs and standard relativistic EMRI waveform modeling, whether the resulting population of PBH-driven EMRIs produces an event rate and signal-to-noise distribution that yields detectable individual events or a resolvable stochastic foreground in the LISA mission. Quantify the predicted detection rate as a function of (i) the central black hole mass, (ii) the assumed PBH mass function, and (iii) the assumed PBH fraction of dark matter, and identify the parameter regions for which detection by LISA is feasible.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a forward-looking research direction concerning the future LISA mission (planned launch in the 2030s) and PBH dark matter scenarios. Studies have begun modeling EMRI rates from PBHs around SMBHs/IMBHs and dark-matter-induced dynamical friction effects on EMRI waveforms, but no definitive answer exists; LISA has not yet collected data and theoretical predictions remain model-dependent. The problem is therefore open.

status_evidence.snippet: Roadmap listing PBH-EMRI detectability in SMBH/IMBH environments as an open question for LISA.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open research question awaiting LISA-era observations and refined theoretical modeling.

status_evidence.title: LISA Mission overview
status_evidence.snippet: LISA is a future ESA-led space-based gravitational-wave observatory targeting launch in the mid-2030s.
status_evidence.claim: LISA has not yet flown, so empirical detectability of PBH-driven EMRIs cannot yet be established.
